Empirical Research Plan:  “How much do parents value school quality?  Evidence from attendance-zone boundaries in suburban Boston, 1993-1995”

------------------------------------------------------------------
1. Identification Strategy
------------------------------------------------------------------
Method:  Spatial Regression Discontinuity Design (RDD), sometimes called a “boundary discontinuity design.”

Rationale
•  Assignment to elementary schools is a deterministic, sharp rule of geography: the home’s latitude/longitude relative to an attendance-zone boundary.  
•  Houses on opposite sides of a boundary share almost every neighborhood attribute except the assigned school.  
•  By comparing sales very near the boundary we can treat the location as a running variable whose sign determines treatment.  
•  This is the cleanest design available; DiD, IV, or RD-DID are unnecessary because the policy does not change over time and assignment has no obvious instrument that would dominate geography.

------------------------------------------------------------------
2. Treatment and Control
------------------------------------------------------------------
Treatment variable
Ti = 1 if house i is assigned to the *higher-quality* school of the two schools that meet at that specific boundary; 0 otherwise.  
(We first rank the paired schools by average 4th-grade MEAP score.  In a robustness check we use per-pupil expenditure.)

Control group
Houses on the *lower-quality* side of the same boundary within a chosen symmetric bandwidth around the border.

Timing / event date
Not applicable—assignment is time-invariant for this period.  We nevertheless control for sale-year fixed effects to absorb overall housing-market trends.

Running variable and cutoff
•  Running variable: signed orthogonal distance (in meters) from the nearest boundary segment.  di > 0 ⇒ higher-quality side; di < 0 ⇒ lower-quality side.  
•  Cutoff: di = 0.

------------------------------------------------------------------
3. Key Identifying Assumptions
------------------------------------------------------------------
A1. Local continuity of potential outcomes  
   E[ln Price0 | di ] and E[ln Price1 | di ] are continuous at di = 0 absent treatment.  
   Plausibility: Within, say, 100–300 m the street grid, crime risk, shopping access, etc. change smoothly; only school assignment jumps.

A2. No precise sorting on the boundary  
   Families cannot costlessly choose a house *precisely* on the preferred side conditional on unobserved willingness-to-pay.  
   Plausibility: Moving costs, search frictions, and the thin housing market limit exact sorting, but we will test density continuity (McCrary).

A3. Boundary fixed characteristics do not correlate with school quality differentially within the bandwidth  
   I.e., parks, rivers, or highways that mechanically define some boundaries are not systematically associated with one side’s school quality.  
   Plausibility: Not guaranteed; we will include boundary-segment fixed effects and check for discontinuities in observables (lot size, house age, crime).

------------------------------------------------------------------
4. Threats to Identification and Mitigation
------------------------------------------------------------------
T1.  Sorting by unobserved household characteristics (e.g., high-income parents buy on the good-school side).  
   Mitigation:  
   •  Density test (McCrary) for manipulation of di.  
   •  Balance tests: run the same RD on predetermined house attributes and census tract demographics; expect no discontinuity.  
   •  Very narrow bandwidths (e.g., 100 m, 200 m) where sorting is least feasible.

T2.  Other discontinuous amenities coincide with the boundary (parks, zoning rules, highway).  
   Mitigation:  
   •  Manually inspect GIS maps for “obvious” amenity breaks; drop those segments in a robustness exercise.  
   •  Control flexibly for distance to the nearest major road, park, or water body.  
   •  Boundary fixed effects so identification comes only from within-boundary contrasts.

T3.  Functional-form mistakes or bandwidth sensitivity.  
   Mitigation:  
   •  Use local linear regressions with triangular kernel (rdrobust default).  
   •  Report results for multiple bandwidth selectors (Imbens-Kalyanaraman, Calonico-Cattaneo-Titiunik).  
   •  Show binned scatterplots of residualized log prices against di.

------------------------------------------------------------------
5. R Code Outline
------------------------------------------------------------------
```r
# ---------------------------------------------------------------
# 0. Packages
# ---------------------------------------------------------------
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)            # spatial
library(rdrobust)      # main RD
library(fixest)        # boundary FE robustness
# ---------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Data loading
# ---------------------------------------------------------------
sales  <- read_csv("ma_sales_93_95.csv")         # house sales
schools <- read_csv("school_quality.csv")        # MEAP scores etc.
boundaries <- st_read("attendance_boundaries.shp") # GIS polygons
# ---------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Variable construction
# ---------------------------------------------------------------
# Merge school quality to boundaries, create ‘better’ flag
boundaries <- boundaries %>% 
  mutate(school_quality = MEAP_score,        # assume field exists
         boundary_id   = row_number())

# Spatial join: assign each sale to a boundary + distance
sales_sf <- st_as_sf(sales, coords = c("lon","lat"), crs = 4326)
sales_sf <- st_transform(sales_sf, st_crs(boundaries))
nearest <- st_nearest_points(sales_sf, boundaries)  # line to boundary
sales_sf$dist_signed <- st_length(nearest) * 
                        ifelse(sales_sf$school_id == boundaries$better_school,1,-1)
# Treatment indicator
sales_sf$T <- ifelse(sales_sf$dist_signed > 0, 1, 0)

# Outcome
sales_sf$ln_price <- log(sales_sf$sale_price)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Main RD regression (Calonico et al. 2014 bias-corrected)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------
# Narrow the data to ±500 m
rd_dat <- sales_sf %>% filter(abs(dist_signed) <= 500)

main_rd <- rdrobust(y = rd_dat$ln_price,
                    x = rd_dat$dist_signed,
                    covs = select(rd_dat, sqft, rooms, age),  # optional
                    cluster = rd_dat$boundary_id)

summary(main_rd)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Robustness: boundary FE difference-in-means inside small bins
# ---------------------------------------------------------------
# Create 50-m bins and keep ±250 m
fe_dat <- sales_sf %>% filter(abs(dist_signed) <= 250) %>%
  mutate(bin = cut(dist_signed, breaks = seq(-250,250,50)))

robust_fe <- feols(ln_price ~ T + sqft + rooms + age | boundary_id + bin, 
                   data = fe_dat, cluster = ~boundary_id)
summary(robust_fe)

# Density test
mccrary <- rddensity(rd_dat$dist_signed)
summary(mccrary)
```

------------------------------------------------------------------
6. Expected Results
------------------------------------------------------------------
Economic intuition and prior estimates (e.g., Black 1999) suggest a *positive* discontinuity: homes assigned to a school whose average MEAP score is 1 SD higher should sell for about 2–4 percent more, holding everything else constant.  With a median 1994 sale price of roughly \$230,000, that implies a \$4,600–\$9,200 premium.

------------------------------------------------------------------
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (RDD)
------------------------------------------------------------------
C1: Continuity of potential outcomes at the cutoff ………………… 0.8  
C2: No precise manipulation of running variable …………………… 0.9  
C3: Sufficient observations close to cutoff ………………………… 0.9  
C4: Correct functional-form / bandwidth choice …………………… 0.7  
C5: Placebo & covariate balance tests passed …………………… 0.8  

(1 = clearly satisfied, 0 = questionable/absent; values represent my confidence)

------------------------------------------------------------------
End of Plan
